general_information.Description: The course describes the corporation and its operating environment, the manner in which corporate boards and management evaluate investment opportunities and arrangements for financing such investments. It also brings discussion in wide range context under varying conditions of aggregate demand, inflation, tax rates, interest rates, among other variables as well as the tools for valuing the short-term movements in bond and equity valuations in the various stock markets are even more complexly determined. Topics include: - Introduction to corporate finance; - Financial statements and how they are related, as well as how these statements are related to cash fl ows to investors; - Ratio analysis and other tools used to evaluate financial statements; - The Time Value of Money and then applies present value concepts to bond and stock valuation; - The principle tool for evaluating capital projects and alternative capital budgeting decision rules; - How project cash flows are calculated and forecast.
general_information.StudentTasks: '- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand the goals of the corporations and roles of financial managers
Understanding of the relationship between risk and return
Understand and employ investment criteria in making investment decisions
Apply different evaluation techniques in pricing bonds and stocks and cash-flow
Using financial analyzing techniques to evaluate a project
Understand techniques to calculate and forecast project cash flows and costs of capital
Apply critical thinking, problem solving, practice ability to work collaboratively within a team and presentation skills to individual and/or group activities dealing with corporate finance
